questions.question: The LDAP connection test succeeds, but Add New does not display 'Loaded from Directory' for a user. What should be checked next?

options.text: Import the user's LDAP group before creating the local account
options.feedback: The recent FortiNAC-F tip states that group import is not required merely to read the user; the user DN must be readable.

options.text: Change the host's access VLAN to the production network
options.feedback: VLAN placement is downstream of identity lookup and cannot make an LDAP user DN readable.

options.text: Check user ID and LDAP read permission on the DN
options.feedback: Correct. A successful bind does not prove the service account can read the specific user DN or that the entered ID matches.

options.text: Disable scheduled directory synchronization for that user
options.feedback: Synchronization is not the first boundary for an Add New lookup that fails to populate directory fields.

questions.question: A user record shows 'Loaded from Directory' and has a role, but the endpoint policy still sees an unknown user. What is the most likely missing relationship?

options.text: The imported user is not linked to the correct host record
options.feedback: Correct. FortiNAC separates user and host objects; the host must be edited and the user explicitly associated.

options.text: The LDAP server is not acting as the DHCP relay service
options.feedback: LDAP supplies identity data; DHCP relay is not the relationship between a user and a FortiNAC host.

options.text: The user's directory group was not imported into FortiGate
options.feedback: The tip notes group import is unnecessary for the user lookup; the missing link is usually the host association.

options.text: The FortiNAC-F switch profile is missing an IGMP querier
options.feedback: IGMP snooping has no role in user-to-host identity association.

questions.question: Is importing the entire LDAP group hierarchy required to manually read one user's directory record?

options.text: Yes; FortiNAC requires a complete group import before user lookup
options.feedback: The Community procedure explicitly says the group does not need to be imported just to read the user.

options.text: No; FortiNAC must be able to read the user's DN
options.feedback: Correct. The LDAP connection must exist and the user DN must be readable; group import is not the prerequisite for this task.

options.text: Only when the endpoint uses a static IPv4 address
options.feedback: IP addressing does not determine whether a user DN can be read from LDAP.

options.text: Only when the user is assigned an administrator profile
options.feedback: The procedure assigns a FortiNAC role after the user is loaded; it does not require an administrator profile for every user.

questions.question: A manually created user ID matches a directory user ID. What can a later directory synchronization do?

options.text: Delete the matching host and all network adapters
options.feedback: The documentation does not say a matching user ID deletes host adapters as part of ordinary synchronization.

options.text: Convert the directory user into a local-only identity
options.feedback: A matching ID preserves the directory relationship; it does not automatically convert the user to local-only authentication.

options.text: Remove the user role and clear all group membership
options.feedback: The documented behavior is directory data refresh, not automatic removal of role and group assignments.

options.text: Overwrite directory-owned user fields with the directory values
options.feedback: Correct. FortiNAC matches by User ID and refreshes fields such as name and email from the directory; manual edits to those fields can be overwritten.

questions.question: On a FortiAuthenticator build before 8.0.4, an EAP-TTLS client has no separate OTP prompt and the RADIUS log reports a missing token. What legacy workaround is documented?

options.text: Enter the LDAP password immediately followed by the current OTP
options.feedback: Correct for the documented pre-8.0.4 behavior. The inner credential is submitted in one field because challenge-based EAP-TTLS 2FA is not supported in that release family.

options.text: Send the OTP as a second RADIUS username attribute
options.feedback: The documented workaround is password-plus-OTP concatenation in the password field, not a second username attribute.

options.text: Disable the EAP-TTLS TLS tunnel and send PAP in clear text
options.feedback: The TLS tunnel protects the inner authentication. Disabling it would weaken security and does not implement the supported workaround.

options.text: Move the FortiToken assignment to the FortiGate user object
options.feedback: The token is assigned and validated by FortiAuthenticator in this design; moving it to FortiGate does not fix the missing EAP-TTLS challenge.

questions.question: A FortiAuthenticator 8.0.4 deployment is being migrated from the older EAP-TTLS concatenation workaround. What should the engineer do?

options.text: Keep concatenation because EAP-TTLS still lacks OTP challenges
options.feedback: That describes the older documentation boundary, but Fortinet's October 2026 update states support is available from 8.0.4.

options.text: Move every user to EAP-MSCHAPv2 without testing client support
options.feedback: Changing EAP methods alters the authentication protocol and client compatibility; it is not the documented 8.0.4 EAP-TTLS update.

options.text: Use 8.0.4 challenge-based EAP-TTLS and verify policy support
options.feedback: Correct. The version update says not to use the legacy concatenation workaround on 8.0.4; validate the new policy flow and supported client versions.

options.text: Remove the FortiAuthenticator EAP server certificate from policy
options.feedback: The TLS server certificate remains part of EAP-TTLS; removing it would break server authentication rather than enable OTP challenge behavior.

questions.question: FortiAuthenticator is configured as a RADIUS proxy to a remote server. Which statement about its local EAP settings is correct?

options.text: Local EAP settings always override the remote server's EAP policy
options.feedback: The documentation says local EAP settings apply to sessions terminated by FortiAuthenticator, not sessions proxied to a remote RADIUS server.

options.text: Local EAP settings apply only when FortiAuthenticator terminates the EAP session
options.feedback: Correct. If EAP is proxied, troubleshoot the remote RADIUS server's EAP configuration and trust path.

options.text: Local EAP settings are used only for MAC authentication bypass
options.feedback: MAB is a separate authentication type; EAP termination/proxy behavior determines which EAP settings apply.

options.text: Local EAP settings are selected by the FortiGate firewall policy ID
options.feedback: The RADIUS client and matching policy determine the authentication flow; the firewall policy ID does not select FAC EAP termination.

questions.question: LDAP authentication succeeds in a standalone test, but IKEv2 EAP-TTLS still fails. Which evidence is most useful next?

options.text: The workstation's DHCP lease and local DNS resolver settings
options.feedback: A lease proves network addressing, not the EAP inner method or second-factor transaction.

options.text: The FortiGate SD-WAN rule order for the VPN destination
options.feedback: SD-WAN path selection may affect reachability, but it does not prove the RADIUS policy and EAP exchange completed.

options.text: The FortiAuthenticator DNS cache and LDAP lookup timeout
options.feedback: DNS may affect server reachability, but the direct LDAP test already narrows the next investigation to the RADIUS/EAP flow.

options.text: Correlate EAP method, RADIUS policy, realm and token result
options.feedback: Correct. A direct LDAP test does not prove that the supplicant used the expected inner method or submitted the second factor.

questions.question: An SSH-key secret must use certificate-based authentication rather than a raw public key. Which secret field choice is required?

options.text: Select Public key with certificate in the SSH-key secret template
options.feedback: Correct. FortiPAM documents this option for FortiProduct (SSH Key) and Unix Account (SSH Key) templates.

options.text: Use a standard public key and attach a separate certificate file
options.feedback: A standard public key does not select the certificate-based SSH mode; use the dedicated Public key with certificate option.

options.text: Choose a Certificate template without any private-key material
options.feedback: The Certificate template stores a certificate artifact; it is not the SSH-key template's public-key authentication selector.

options.text: Use an associated secret with a password-only SSH credential
options.feedback: Associated secrets can supply launch credentials, but they do not change the SSH key's certificate authentication type.

questions.question: FortiPAM shows a valid SSH certificate in Secret Details, but the target rejects the launch. What does the display fail to prove?

options.text: That FortiPAM stored a credential for the configured SSH account
options.feedback: The validity display proves that certificate metadata is present in the secret; the question is about target-side acceptance.

options.text: That the certificate includes a valid expiration date
options.feedback: The validity period is displayed, so expiry metadata is visible. The remaining issue is the target's trust and principal policy.

options.text: That the target trusts the CA and accepts the certificate principal
options.feedback: Correct. FortiPAM's certificate status does not prove the target's trusted-CA configuration or authorized principal mapping.

options.text: That the secret can be opened in the FortiPAM UI
options.feedback: The UI display proves the object can be viewed; it does not establish the target SSH server's trust decision.

questions.question: Where are email notifications for expiring SSH certificates configured?

options.text: In the secret's launcher command and connection settings
options.feedback: Launcher settings control how the target session starts, not certificate expiry notifications.

options.text: In the Certificate tab of Email Alert Settings
options.feedback: Correct. FortiPAM documents certificate expiry notifications in the Certificate tab of Email Alert Settings.

options.text: In FortiPAM's HA heartbeat and failover configuration
options.feedback: HA heartbeat monitors appliance availability and is unrelated to certificate expiry email alerts.

options.text: In the target Unix account's password and login policy
options.feedback: Password policy controls password generation/rotation; it does not configure certificate email notifications.

questions.question: Which distinction matters when storing an SSH certificate in FortiPAM?

options.text: Both secret types store identical key material; only the label differs
options.feedback: The templates have different semantics and fields; they should not be treated as interchangeable.

options.text: The Certificate template is required for all SSH key secrets
options.feedback: The SSH-key template has its own Public key with certificate option; the generic Certificate template stores a certificate artifact.

options.text: The SSH-key template hides certificate validity from Secret Details
options.feedback: FortiPAM documents certificate details and validity status for SSH-key secrets using the certificate public-key option.

options.text: SSH-key stores a login key; Certificate stores a certificate file
options.feedback: Correct. Keep the SSH credential mode separate from a general certificate-file secret that may include private-key/passphrase fields.

questions.question: LDAPS authentication fails only when Check Certificate is enabled. The LDAP server certificate is issued to ldap01.example.com, but the profile uses 10.20.30.40. What is the likely cause?

options.text: FortiSIEM requires LDAP servers to listen on TCP port 1812
options.feedback: TCP/1812 is commonly associated with RADIUS, not the LDAP certificate name check.

options.text: The Base DN must include the LDAP server's certificate hostname
options.feedback: Base DN identifies directory search scope; it does not resolve the TLS certificate identity mismatch.

options.text: The profile hostname does not match the certificate CN/SAN
options.feedback: Correct. FortiSIEM checks the certificate CN or SAN against the LDAP host/IP entered in the profile.

options.text: The user must be a System Admin before LDAP can bind
options.feedback: Role assignment affects FortiSIEM authorization after authentication, not the TLS name check against the LDAP server.

questions.question: A SAML IdP authenticates a user, but FortiSIEM grants the wrong tenant role. What should be inspected?

options.text: Exact user match and SAML organization/role mappings to FortiSIEM values
options.feedback: Correct. FortiSIEM requires exact case-sensitive user matching and explicit mapping of IdP organization/role to FortiSIEM scope.

options.text: The Collector's syslog listener and event forwarding configuration
options.feedback: Collector event ingestion does not determine the user's SAML role or organization mapping.

options.text: The event worker's ClickHouse shard and storage placement
options.feedback: Event storage placement is unrelated to SAML user authorization.

options.text: The Supervisor's log retention and tenant partition settings
options.feedback: Retention controls stored event history, not the identity provider's role and tenant mapping.

questions.question: The external authentication profile's Test function succeeds, but the user still sees the wrong FortiSIEM pages. Which check is next?

options.text: Increase the provider's LDAP timeout and connection retry interval
options.feedback: The Test already succeeds; the issue may be user binding or authorization rather than provider reachability.

options.text: Bind the CMDB user to the profile, role and organization
options.feedback: Correct. Profile connectivity does not prove the local user object maps to the correct role and tenant.

options.text: Rebuild the FortiSIEM event database and query cache
options.feedback: The event database does not assign user roles or organization scope.

options.text: Change the username to include the domain suffix twice
options.feedback: Credential formatting may affect authentication, but the successful test and wrong page visibility point to authorization mapping.

questions.question: A user has two external authentication profiles. The first server is contacted successfully but rejects the credentials. What happens?

options.text: FortiSIEM continues to the next profile as a credential fallback
options.feedback: The documented behavior does not treat an authentication rejection as a simple fallback to another profile.

options.text: FortiSIEM disables the local user until an administrator resets it
options.feedback: The profile sequence does not imply an automatic local account disable action.

options.text: FortiSIEM chooses the profile with the newest certificate
options.feedback: Profile selection follows the configured sequence and connection/authentication result, not certificate age.

options.text: The authentication process ends after the contacted server rejects the user
options.feedback: Correct. Multiple profiles are contacted sequentially until a connection succeeds; once a server is contacted and authentication fails, the process ends.

questions.question: A threat feed exists in FortiManager but does not appear in FortiSASE after synchronization. What is the first configuration check?

options.text: Check whether the feed URL uses a public address
options.feedback: Reachability may matter after the feed is synchronized, but the documented sync prerequisite is profile association.

options.text: Confirm every FortiGate in the ADOM is authorized in FortiAnalyzer
options.feedback: FortiAnalyzer authorization is unrelated to FortiManager-to-FortiSASE feed synchronization.

options.text: Confirm a Web Filter or DNS Filter profile references the feed
options.feedback: Correct. Only external feeds associated with Web Filter or DNS Filter profiles are synchronized.

options.text: Check whether the feed URL is present in a static route
options.feedback: A static route does not bind the threat feed to a supported filter profile.

questions.question: An external feed requires HTTP Basic Authentication. FortiManager sync succeeds, but FortiSASE cannot download entries. What is the missing step?

options.text: Recreate the FortiManager ADOM with a new name
options.feedback: ADOM naming does not transfer the Basic Authentication credentials.

options.text: Enter the feed username and password directly in FortiSASE
options.feedback: Correct. Fortinet documents that Basic Authentication credentials configured in FortiManager are not synchronized.

options.text: Add the feed URL to the FortiGate DNS database
options.feedback: DNS resolution does not supply the HTTP authentication credentials required by the feed server.

options.text: Disable SSL inspection for every SASE policy
options.feedback: SSL inspection is not the documented missing credential step and broad disabling would be an unsafe workaround.

questions.question: A feed card is visible in FortiSASE and contains the expected domains, but a test URL is allowed. What should be checked next?

options.text: The remote category action, profile group and traffic policy binding
options.feedback: Correct. Feed entries are data; enforcement requires the correct Web/DNS profile action and a policy that uses the profile.

options.text: The FortiManager administrator's password expiry and account status
options.feedback: The feed has already synchronized and contains entries; the remaining issue is likely profile/action binding.

options.text: The user's wireless airtime weight and SSID assignment
options.feedback: Wireless scheduling has no role in a FortiSASE Web/DNS category decision.

options.text: The FortiGate VIP ARP reply and external interface mapping
options.feedback: VIP ARP ownership is unrelated to SASE filter category enforcement.

questions.question: Which feed-count statement matches the FortiSASE 26.1.107 documentation?

options.text: A maximum of 21 external-host feeds, with no domain feeds
options.feedback: The documented 21 limit applies to DNS Filter Domains and Web Filter FQDNs; external-host feeds are excluded.

options.text: A maximum of 20 feeds across all feed types
options.feedback: That is not the stated limit for the DNS-domain/Web-FQDN synchronization workflow in this guide.

options.text: An unlimited number of feeds if FortiManager is the controller
options.feedback: FortiManager central management does not remove the documented category ID limit.

options.text: Up to 21 DNS-domain and Web-FQDN feeds; external-host feeds are excluded
options.feedback: Correct. The guide identifies category IDs 201–221 inclusive for the 21-feed limit and excludes external-host feeds from the count.

questions.question: Four IPsec overlays share two physical WAN links. The service uses bibandwidth but still evaluates each overlay independently. What setting changes the bandwidth reference to the shared physical link?

options.text: Set mode to manual and remove the health check
options.feedback: That changes service eligibility logic and removes SLA input; it does not select underlay bandwidth.

options.text: Set bandwidth-type underlay in the SD-WAN service
options.feedback: Correct. The default is overlay; underlay mode makes the load-balance service use shared physical underlay bandwidth.

options.text: Enable packet duplication on every overlay member
options.feedback: Duplication sends copies of traffic; it is not the bandwidth accounting selector.

options.text: Set the health-check server to the ISP gateway
options.feedback: The probe target affects health measurement, not whether the load-balance hash uses overlay or underlay capacity.

questions.question: Which hash mode uses the member's available bandwidth in both incoming and outgoing directions?

options.text: source-ip-based
options.feedback: Source-IP hashing pins traffic from a source to a member; it does not compare bidirectional available bandwidth.

options.text: outbandwidth
options.feedback: Outbandwidth selects using available outgoing bandwidth only.

options.text: bibandwidth
options.feedback: Correct. Bibandwidth evaluates available bandwidth for both incoming and outgoing traffic.

options.text: round-robin
options.feedback: Round-robin distributes traffic in circular order and does not use available bandwidth as its hash metric.

questions.question: A service has load-balance enabled and hash-mode bibandwidth, but the members still show overlay capacity. Which setting is missing?

options.text: bandwidth-type underlay
options.feedback: Correct. The default bandwidth-type is overlay; explicitly set underlay to use shared physical capacity.

options.text: update-static-route enable
options.feedback: Static-route update controls route installation based on health-check state, not bandwidth accounting type.

options.text: set priority-members to all members
options.feedback: The priority list determines eligible members; it does not change overlay versus underlay bandwidth measurement.

options.text: set mode to manual
options.feedback: Manual mode changes SLA selection behavior and is not the underlay bandwidth selector.

questions.question: After setting bandwidth-type underlay, which command provides the documented service/member evidence?

options.text: diagnose sys sdwan health-check
options.feedback: Health-check output helps establish SLA state but does not show the selected service's bandwidth hash/member result.

options.text: get router info routing-table all
options.feedback: The routing table shows route selection, not the service's bandwidth-type and per-member bibandwidth evidence.

options.text: diagnose firewall iprope list
options.feedback: Policy lookup output is not the documented SD-WAN service bandwidth inspection.

options.text: diagnose sys sdwan service4
options.feedback: Correct. The example uses this command to inspect service mode, member bandwidth values and selected members.

questions.question: Two overlay members share the same best underlay bandwidth value and both appear selected. What should the engineer infer?

options.text: FortiGate is splitting every packet across both tunnels
options.feedback: The output does not establish per-packet striping; load balancing selects eligible members for session distribution.

options.text: Both members are eligible; tie-break/configuration order can determine preference
options.feedback: Correct. The example notes configuration-order tie-break behavior when values are equal; inspect sessions and service selection rather than assuming packet striping.

options.text: The SLA health check has been disabled automatically
options.feedback: Equal bandwidth values do not indicate that the health check is disabled.

options.text: Underlay bandwidth mode is not active on either member
options.feedback: Both selected members can still reflect underlay bandwidth; equal values alone do not mean the setting failed.
